newsitem.title: USA: CSW, Entergy propose lower Cajun rates.
newsitem.headline: CSW, Entergy propose lower Cajun rates.

text.p: Southwestern Electric Power Co and Entergy Gulf States have proposed the lowest initial rate and new, flexible pricing options for Louisiana's distribution cooperatives under their reorganization plan for Cajun Electric Power Cooperative Inc, Southwestern said on Thursday.

The new proposal supports the second amended plan filed in bankruptcy court on October 26 by the Central and South West Corp and Entergy Corp subsidiaries along with the members committee, which currently consists of seven of the 12 distribution cooperatives served by Cajun.

During a March 3 Louisiana Public Service Commission (LPSC) hearing on the rate provisions of the three competing proposals, SWEPCO representatives said the company's proposal would provide an average initial wholesale rate of less than $0.0345 per kilowatt-hour.

"This represents a reduction of at least 20 percent from existing rates paid by the cooperatives to Cajun," said Marvin McGregor, SWEPCO's Cajun Electric project manager, after the hearing. "Our plan would provide the lowest initial rate of the three competing plans."
In addition, under proposed contracts with the member cooperatives, the SWEPCO plan would be the lowest-cost plan over a 10-, 15- or 25-year time horizon, McGregor said.

"For example, the SWEPCO plan offers 15-year present value savings for the cooperatives of $82 million as compared to the Enron (Corp ) plan, and $173 million as compared to the (Northern States Power Co's ) NRG Energy, Zeigler Coal Holding Co and Southern (Co ) plan," he said.
The commission has used a 15-year period for analysis in its continuing review of wholesale rates in the competing bankruptcy plans, the SWEPCO statement said.

"Under our proposal, each co-op would be able to choose a rate option that varies with fuel prices, starting at an average of less than $0.0345 per kilowatt-hour and guaranteed not to exceed an average of $0.036 in the first year," McGregor said. "Or they would be able to choose a fixed-rate option of $0.038 for 10 years."

Under either of the proposed rates, each member cooperative would preserve the option, at five-year intervals, to move from a fixed rate to an actual fuel cost rate, or from an actual fuel cost rate to a new fixed rate.

The members also would have market flexibility under the SWEPCO proposal through provisions that would allow the cooperatives to shop for power on the open market when their combined energy needs exceed a certain level, or to buy additional power from SWEPCO at the same rate as their base supply rate within certain contract parameters.

Under the proposal put forward with Entergy, SWEPCO would acquire all of Cajun's non-nuclear assets, including the Big Cajun I natural gas-fired plant and the Big Cajun II coal- fired plant for about $780 million in cash, up to an $20 million more to pay certain other bankruptcy claims, and $7 million to acquire claims of unsecured creditors.
